body:
Part of the E127 umbrella (#1183). Architect (2026-09-29): Formal AI must "answer any questions, do summaries, translation, formalization, and all the list of features that are commonly expected from the AI"; parity class **formalization** (tracked as a class in #1171/E136). `formal-ai chat --silent --prompt "Formalize in first-order logic: Every student who studies passes the exam."` (0.347.0) returns the canned search paragraph instead of a formalization, even though two internal formalization mechanisms already exist in the tree.

## Evidence

- **PROMPT:** `Formalize in first-order logic: Every student who studies passes the exam.` **ANSWER:** `Web search requested for `Formalize in first-order logic: Every student who studies passes the exam`. In the browser demo formal-ai defaults to the DuckDuckGo Instant Answer endpoint …` — the fixed paragraph from `rust/src/solver_handlers/web_requests.rs` (see #1173/E138), not a formalization. This is the same routing-fallthrough root cause #1173 (E138) and #1175 (E140) already document for other classes.
- **Why it falls through, precisely.** `try_translation` (`rust/src/solver_handlers/mod.rs:239-260`) is the only handler that reads `crate::translation::formal_language_in_prompt` (line 253). It gates on `is_translation_request = head_initial_command || head_final_command || source_first_command || define_in_links` (line ~300), and every one of those four conditions requires a *translation* verb from the `translation_action` role (`data/seed/meanings-translation.lino:114`) — "translate", "переведи", etc. "Formalize" is not a member of that role (verified: `git grep -n "formaliz" data/seed/meanings-translation.lino` finds nothing). So `is_translation_request` is `false`, `try_translation` returns `None` at line ~260, and the prompt never reaches the formal-language branch at all — it falls through to the search handler further down `solver.rs`.
- **Even if routed, the mechanism can only render one triple shape.** `rust/src/translation/formal_statement.rs` (425 lines) defines `SemanticStatement { subject, predicate, object }` — a single atomic Wikidata-anchored triple. `parse_natural_statement`/`parse_formal_statement` require both `subject` and `object` to resolve to a `ROLE_WIKIDATA_ENTITY_ANCHOR` meaning and `predicate` to a `ROLE_BINARY_RELATION_PROPERTY` meaning (lines 199-260). `data/seed/formal-language-projections.lino` (27 lines, confirmed in full) seeds exactly one relation, `P31` ("is a"), with the FOL template `"{predicate}({subject}, {object})"` and one natural-language template per `en/ru/hi/zh/es`. There is no quantifier, no variable, no clause, no implication anywhere in the schema or the code — "Every student who studies passes the exam" is a universal-quantifier conditional (∀x (Student(x) ∧ Studies(x) → Passes(x))) with no Wikidata-entity subject or object, so `translate_statement` would return `UnrecognizedStatement` even if the routing gate let it through.
- **The unresolved-need formalizer is a different machine, for different input.** `rust/src/formalization/` (`mod.rs`, `segment.rs`, `needs.rs`, `concepts.rs`, `concept_links.rs`, `procedures.rs`) is "deep formalization: segmentation, need emission, concept grounding, procedure extraction" for text **retrieved during research** (issue #1138 plan 04); `needs.rs:1-20` states it formalizes documents the solver fetched, raising `Need`s for unresolved surfaces. It is not wired to a user's own sentence and has no FOL/Lean/Rocq rendering.
- **The proof engine has no formula representation either.** `rust/src/proof_engine/types.rs` (273 lines, read in full) defines `ProofMethod`, `StepKind`, `ProofStep`, `Proof`, `ProofOutcome`, `ProofRenderConfig` — proof *methods* and *steps*, not a `Formula`/`Statement`/`Quantifier` type. `ProofMethod::DecisionProcedure`'s doc comment ("Delegate to the relative-meta-logic / SMT-style decision procedure") is the only mention of relative-meta-logic in the engine, and it is unimplemented delegation, not a formula type. `try_proof_request` (`rust/src/solver_handlers/user_intent.rs`) triggers on "prove …"/"show that …", not "formalize …".
- **No Lean/Rocq bridge is vendored.** `rust/Cargo.toml` has no `meta-logic`/`rml`/`relative-meta-logic` dependency (checked: no match). `link-foundation/relative-meta-logic`'s README documents `rml export lean <file>.lino -o out.lean` (`docs/LEAN_EXPORT.md`, "typed, non-probabilistic RML fragments") and `rml export rocq <file.lino> -o <file.v>` (`docs/ROCQ-EXPORT.md`, "the supported typed LiNo subset"), plus dependent-types kernel rules for `Pi`/`lambda`/`apply` (`docs/KERNEL.md`) — runnable from its repository (`node js/src/rml-links.mjs export lean …`, `cargo run -- export lean …`) but not published; link-foundation/relative-meta-logic#185 tracks `link-foundation/relative-meta-logic#185 (publish; light probability core)` as a prerequisite for an in-process integration.

## What to build

- **Routing.** Add `formalize`/`формализуй`/`औपचारिक बनाओ`/`形式化` as a `formalization_command` role (parallel to `translation_action`) in a new/extended seed file, and a `data/seed/capability-routing.lino` `route` entry: `object formalization_target`, `act formalize`, `locus request_text`, `capability formalize_statement`. A new handler `try_formalization_request` runs before the search fallback, mirroring `try_translation`'s position in `solver_handlers/mod.rs`.
- **Quantified statement schema.** Extend `data/seed/formal-language-projections.lino` with a `clause` layer above the existing triple: a `quantifier` (`forall`/`exists`), a bound `variable`, one or more `predicate` applications over that variable joined by `conjunction`/`disjunction`, and an optional `implication` to a consequent clause. Example target shape for the probe sentence:
  ```lino
  formal_language "fol"
    clause_template "{quantifier}{variable} ({antecedent} {implies} {consequent})"
    quantifier forall
      symbol "∀"
    connective implies
      symbol "→"
    connective and
      symbol "∧"
  ```
  with the parsed instance `∀x (Student(x) ∧ Studies(x) → Passes(x))` carrying `Student`/`Studies`/`Passes` as predicate meanings (new role, not `ROLE_WIKIDATA_ENTITY_ANCHOR`, since they are class/verb predicates over a bound variable, not Wikidata items).
- **Rendering.** Extend `rust/src/translation/formal_statement.rs`'s template engine (`render_template`/`match_template`) to compose nested clause templates recursively instead of one flat triple. FOL text renders through the existing seeded template mechanism; Lean/Rocq render in-process through the `relative-meta-logic` Rust crate's export (the same code `rml export lean|rocq` runs), added as a git source dependency per CONTRIBUTING "Self-maintained dependencies and patches" with a comment linking link-foundation/relative-meta-logic#185 beside it; switched to the crates.io release when #185 publishes.
- **Round trip.** Deformalization (FOL/Lean/Rocq text → natural-language sentence) reuses `rust/src/formalization/segment.rs`'s clause segmentation and `translation::formal_statement`'s render-in-reverse path, checked for meaning equivalence against the original prompt.
- **Multilingual.** en/ru/hi/zh/es, matching the existing `natural_language` blocks' word order (`{subject} {predicate} {object}` for en/ru/es, `{subject} {object} {predicate}` for hi, `{subject}{predicate}{object}` for zh) extended with the quantifier/connective slot.

## Requirements

R1. A prompt containing a formalization-command surface ("formalize", "формализуй", "औपचारिक बनाओ में", "形式化") in en/ru/hi/zh routes to `try_formalization_request` before the search fallback, never producing the canned "Web search requested" paragraph.
R2. `try_formalization_request` parses a sentence containing a universal or existential quantifier, at least one conjunction, and an implication (e.g. "Every X that Ys Zs") into a nested clause structure — not only the single-triple `SemanticStatement`.
R3. The parsed clause renders to FOL text using the `∀`/`∃`/`∧`/`∨`/`→` symbols declared in the seed, matching the shape `∀x (P(x) ∧ Q(x) → R(x))` for a two-antecedent universal conditional.
R4. The same parsed clause renders to Lean 4 and Rocq source through the relative-meta-logic crate's export functions (in-process), and the outputs are checked: when `lean`/`coqc` is available in the environment the files compile; otherwise the answer states which check was not run.
R5. Deformalization renders the FOL/Lean/Rocq form back to a natural-language sentence in the original request language, and the round trip preserves the quantifier, the predicates and the implication (checked by re-parsing the rendered sentence and comparing clause structure, not string equality).
R6. `formal-ai explain <answer>` prints the derivation: parsed clause, chosen template, rendered target, and (when invoked) the `rml` exit status and output path — the white-box contract from #1183 acceptance criterion 2.
R7. Three-roots parity: the handler is translated with `formal-ai translate --from rust --to js|ts --input <file> --write` (relative-meta-logic also ships a JS implementation, `js/src/rml-links.mjs`, for the JS root's export), and `data/parity/cross-runtime-synthesis.json` gains formalization cases answered identically by all three roots.
R8. `docs/llm-task-parity.md`'s "formalization" row (#1171/E136) shows a useful, verified answer for the probe set, replacing the current "canned web-search paragraph" status.
R9. No formalization is memorized per-input: the no-memorization gate (`tests/unit/coding_discovery/no_memorization.rs`) is extended to scan the new clause seed/runtime for a hardcoded whole-sentence FOL string keyed to a specific probe prompt.

## Design

New:
- `rust/src/solver_handlers/formalization_request.rs` — the handler; entry gate, clause parse, dispatch to FOL/Lean/Rocq renderers.
- `rust/src/formal_export.rs` — calls the relative-meta-logic crate's Lean/Rocq export in-process and records the rendered file hashes as evidence.
- `data/benchmarks/formalization/{en,ru,hi,zh}.lino` — probe set (schema below).
- `rust/tests/unit/issue_1186_formalization_request.rs`, registered as `mod issue_1186_formalization_request;` in `rust/tests/unit/mod.rs` (alongside the existing `mod issue_1138_formalization_depth;` at line 62 and `mod issue_1138_translation_tool;` at line 71, which cover the retrieved-document formalizer and the CLI translate tool respectively — this is a third, sibling module for the user-facing case).

Modified:
- `data/seed/formal-language-projections.lino` — add `quantifier`, `connective` and `clause_template` records (27 lines today).
- `data/seed/meanings-translation.lino` or a new `data/seed/meanings-formalization-command.lino` — the `formalization_command` role and its per-language surfaces (mirrors `role translation_action` at line 114).
- `data/seed/capability-routing.lino` — the new `route` entry (mirrors the `object url / act retrieve` entries already in the file).
- `rust/src/translation/formal_statement.rs` — extend `SemanticStatement`/`render_template`/`match_template` for nested clauses (currently strictly `{subject, predicate, object}`, lines 17-30 and 316-360).
- `rust/src/solver_handlers/mod.rs` — call the new handler from `solve` alongside `try_translation` (both currently live behind the same general "language handling" region).

## Probe set and tests

`data/benchmarks/formalization/en.lino` (and `ru.lino`/`hi.lino`/`zh.lino`), 10+ prompts each, following the field shape of `data/benchmarks/capability-routing/en.lino` (`record_type`, `id`, `language`, `prompt`, plus formalization-specific fields):

```lino
formalization_case_en_01
  record_type "formalization_case"
  id "en_01"
  language "en"
  prompt "Formalize in first-order logic: Every student who studies passes the exam."
  expected_quantifier "forall"
  expected_predicates ("Student" "Studies" "Passes")
  expected_fol "∀x (Student(x) ∧ Studies(x) → Passes(x))"
  expect_lean_export true
  expect_rocq_export true
```
Held-out prompts cover: universal + existential quantifiers, negation, two-place relations, and multilingual equivalents (e.g. ru "Каждый студент, который учится, сдаёт экзамен", hi "हर छात्र जो पढ़ता है, परीक्षा पास करता है", zh "每个学习的学生都通过考试").

Expected-answer check: the rendered FOL string matches `expected_fol` up to whitespace/symbol normalization; the Lean/Rocq outputs compile when `lean`/`coqc` is present (probed once through `rust/src/prerequisite/probe.rs`; when absent the test records the skipped check with its reason, never a silent pass).

Test file: `rust/tests/unit/issue_1186_formalization_request.rs`. Command: `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.98.1 cargo test --test unit issue_1186_formalization_request`.

`docs/llm-task-parity.md`'s formalization row is regenerated by the same probe-run + `render-status.rs`-style generator #1171/E136 builds for `data/meta/llm-task-classes.lino`; this issue's probe set is the `probe_set_path` that class's row points at.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Requirement shard `docs/requirements/issue-1186-formalization-as-a-user-facing-task.md`, assembled into `REQUIREMENTS.md` via `rust-script scripts/assemble-requirements.rs --write`.
- [ ] `docs/requirements-traceability.md` row per requirement with automated test (R1-R9 above) and manual confirmation.
- [ ] Case study `docs/case-studies/issue-1186/` with the routing-gap audit above, the clause-schema design, and the `rml` CLI survey.
- [ ] Changelog fragment via `rust-script scripts/create-changelog-fragment.rs --bump-type <minor|patch> --description "..."` under `changelog.d/`.
- [ ] `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.98.1 rust-script scripts/run-ci-gates.rs --stage rust` green.
- [ ] No-memorization gate (`tests/unit/coding_discovery/no_memorization.rs`, extended per R9) passes.
- [ ] `docs/llm-task-parity.md`'s formalization row shows a passing, verified probe count (#1171/E136).

## Depends on / blocks

- Depends on #1175 (E140): routing by the formalized request, so "formalize …" reaches this handler.
- Depends on #1173 (E138): the canned search paragraph must no longer be the fallback for everything.
- Uses link-foundation/relative-meta-logic#185 (source dependency now, crates.io release when published) for Lean/Rocq export.
- Feeds #1171 (E136): the formalization row's probe set and formal-version description.
- Records its derivation in #1184 (E148) (R6).
title: E150: formalization as a user-facing task: formalize text into Links Notation, first-order logic, Lean and Rocq (via relative-meta-logic), with round-trip deformalization in en/ru/hi/zh
